title: VSL Settlement Receipt 1.0
description: A signed set of hash commitments describing a validated, authorized, dual-triggered exchange. A Receipt never contains the payload. FROZEN at 1.0 (VSL-PRD §13.3): a Receipt is a long-lived artifact that a third party must be able to check years later against this published schema, so no field may be added, removed or reinterpreted within 1.0.

version.description: Receipt format version. A different value means a different schema; a verifier that does not recognise it must refuse rather than guess.

canonicalization.description: The canonicalization used for every hash in this Receipt. Committed inside receipt_hash so the scheme cannot be reinterpreted under a weaker one. RFC 8785 conformant, not 'aligned': see VSL-PRD §5.2 and sdcgovernance.jcs.

receipt_id.description: CUID2, 24 characters. Assigned when the Receipt is built, therefore known to both parties before either signs a trigger.

timestamp.description: RFC 3339, UTC, Z suffix required. Local offsets are refused so canonical bytes cannot vary by issuer locale.

payload_hash.description: SHA-256 over the canonical payload bytes. The payload itself is never carried.

payload_media_type.description: Media type of the committed payload, e.g. application/xml or application/ld+json.

schema_ct_id.description: CUID2 of the bound component in the catalog.

schema_url.description: Unauthenticated location of the published component (VSL-PRD §5.6). Present so a receiving party who does not run SDC can fetch the schema and re-validate without depending on us.

schema_hash.description: SHA-256 over the published schema bytes, so the fetch at schema_url is checkable.

rm_version.description: Reference model the component was published under. Recorded so a Receipt survives a reference-model change.

recovered.description: True when ExceptionalValues were injected to reach a valid document.

ev_injections.description: ISO 21090 exceptional values injected during recovery. Empty when recovered is false.

validator_version.description: Exact validator build, so step 5 of the verification procedure is reproducible.

provenance_hash.description: SHA-256 over the canonical provenance chain.

receipt_hash.description: receipt_hash of the sdcgovernance Receipt that produced `decision`. A holder of that Receipt can confirm it hashes to this value, re-run sdcgovernance against it, and follow its own previous_hash chain.

receipt_url.description: Unauthenticated location of the governance Receipt, or null when it is not published. Mirrors the schema_ct_id / schema_url / schema_hash pattern in §5.6: a receiving party who holds neither can still fetch and check. Declared now because a frozen format cannot gain it later.

governance.description: The governance verdict AND a commitment to the evidence that produced it. Carrying the decision alone would make it an assertion a verifier cannot check, and would leave the sdcgovernance hash chain unlinked; binding by hash is the join described in VSL-PRD §3.3.

condition_hash.description: SHA-256 over the canonical release condition.

parties.description: Key ids expected to trigger. A settlement completes when every listed party appears in triggers.

triggers.description: Appended after receipt_hash is computed, so triggers are NOT covered by it (see $comment on receipt_hash). Each trigger is independently verifiable and order does not matter.

signature.description: ES256 over the RFC 8785 canonical form of {"condition_hash": ..., "receipt_id": ...}. ★ receipt_id is included deliberately: a signature over condition_hash alone would be replayable into any other Receipt sharing the same release condition. Both values are fixed before either party signs, so independent out-of-order signing is preserved.

previous_hash.description: receipt_hash of the prior Receipt in this chain, or null for the first.

receipt_hash.$comment: SHA-256 over the RFC 8785 canonical form of this object with receipt_hash, signatures and settlement.triggers removed. Triggers are excluded because §5.4 appends them after hashing so the parties can sign independently and out of order; each trigger carries its own signature and is bound to this Receipt through receipt_id.
receipt_hash.description: Integrity commitment over the Receipt content.

signatures.description: Issuer signatures over receipt_hash. Not covered by receipt_hash itself.

alg.description: JOSE algorithm name (RFC 7518 §3.4), which defines ECDSA P-256 with SHA-256 and fixes the signature encoding as the P1363 r||s pair. Naming the JOSE algorithm therefore pins the wire encoding; there is no separate encoding field to disagree about.

sha256.description: SHA-256 as 64 lowercase hex characters. Case is pinned so the value has one canonical form.

key_id.description: Identifier resolvable at /.well-known/sdcstudio-signing-keys.json, or against a key retained earlier. Verification must work from a cached key.

signature.description: ES256 signature: the 64-byte P1363 r||s pair, base64url encoded without padding, which is 86 characters. base64url rather than base64 follows JOSE and keeps the value safe in URLs and headers.
